## Natural history notes

A small pleasing lacewing characterized by delicate clear wings, long threadlike antennae, and a slender brownish body, with males of the group often having comb-like antennae. In Florida, Nallachius americanus is associated with wooded habitats where dead branches, bark, and insect galleries provide protected microhabitats for larvae. Adults may come to lights, while the larvae live in wood or bark galleries and are presumed to prey on eggs and larvae of bark- or wood-inhabiting insects such as beetles and ants, making them part of the hidden predator community in deadwood habitats.
